title: Glacier Shelf — Diagonal Keynote Slab
description: A single angled frosted pane cuts across a saturated teal-to-indigo gradient, stripping a conference title card to pure atmosphere and headline weight. Where most glass templates layer cards and chrome, this one commits to a single unbroken slab and silence.
philosophy: This design exists for the held breath before a talk begins — when a room dims and one slide has to do everything without saying too much. It rejects icon grids, logo lockups, and the visual clutter that signals insecurity. The diagonal composition creates latent energy without chaos, and the near-empty field trusts oversized type to land on its own terms. It is built for large projection screens, low ambient light, and speakers who earn authority through restraint.
goodFor: Opening title slides for 30–60 minute conference keynotes
Single-line or two-line title statements projected in large venues
Speaker introduction cards where name and talk title are the only content
Tech or design conference openers where visual craft signals credibility
avoidFor: Multi-point agenda or section-divider slides requiring scannable lists
Chart-heavy quarterly reviews where data legibility competes with the background
Presentations requiring persistent logo or brand lockup placement
Decks with 20+ slides where the slab motif loses impact through repetition
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the held breath the instant a conference room dims — deep atmospheric gradient receding into distance, a single unbroken frosted slab slicing diagonally through the frame with calm inevitability. The diagonal carries all the latent energy so the type doesn't have to; the headline lands in near-silence and earns its weight from the surrounding void. Composition is asymmetric and sparse, prioritizing cinematic scale over informational density. Avoid layered cards, symmetrical centering, decorative chrome, or anything that fragments the slab's singular authority.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas with no outer margin frame — the gradient occupies the entire field. A single diagonal frosted slab enters from the lower-left edge and exits upper-right, bisecting the slide as the sole structural element. Title text anchors left in the upper zone of a 12-col grid (cols 1–9), sitting above the slab's upper edge to claim the open sky of the composition. A secondary line — subtitle or speaker attribution — rests just below the cut, bottom-left aligned, with an optional event label pinned bottom-right at minimal visual weight.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a single thought projected into a dimly lit auditorium — spare, weighted, deliberate. The frosted diagonal slab contracts from hero coverage into a content-bearing wedge, giving the composition asymmetric tension: meaning anchored on one side, vast atmospheric silence on the other. Rhythm is slow and confident, not modular or grid-locked. Avoid decorative iconography, chrome dividers, or layered card surfaces — content must feel inevitable, as if it could not have been placed any other way.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a 7% outer margin on all sides. The diagonal frosted slab narrows from its full-field hero form into a content-bearing wedge spanning the left-to-center columns, maintaining the same angle as the title slide; primary content — a single quoted statement, lone stat callout, or maximum three-item sparse list — sits entirely within this slab zone, aligned to its left interior edge. Hierarchy is established through weight contrast alone plus a fine horizontal rule separating a short category label from the body content below it. Page number sits bottom-right in the open gradient field; no header band, no persistent logo zone.
